title: Java Comparators: Sort Tasks by Priority
contract: Each task is [priority,id]. Sort higher priority first, then lower id; values may span the full int range.
brute: for(int i=0;i<tasks.length;i++)for(int j=i+1;j<tasks.length;j++)if(tasks[j][0]>tasks[i][0]||(tasks[j][0]==tasks[i][0]&&tasks[j][1]<tasks[i][1])){int[] t=tasks[i];tasks[i]=tasks[j];tasks[j]=t;emit("Select by the two ordering rules","tasks",tasks);}return tasks;
optimal: Comparator<int[]> order=Comparator.<int[]>comparingInt(x->x[0]).reversed().thenComparingInt(x->x[1]);Arrays.sort(tasks,order);for(int i=0;i<tasks.length;i++)emit("Read the sorted priority order","position",i,"task",tasks[i]);return tasks;
reasoning: A nested-loop comparison implements the specification directly but needs quadratic comparisons.
Compose comparator keys so descending priority and ascending id remain independent.
Use comparingInt or Integer.compare instead of subtraction, which can overflow and violate comparator transitivity. Reversing the whole comparator after thenComparing would reverse the tie rule too.
complexity: O(n log n), O(n) sorting workspace
